title: How long is the whole arm of Ruhee?
description: Two arm lengths with units and tenths are added in two ways: first the units and the tenths separately, then as counts of tenths. Keeko doubts the tenths and adds the top numbers and the bottom numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: tenths of the same size are added by adding their counts, and the size stays tenths. Watch for students who add the bottom numbers too and get twentieths.

source: The lower arm is 2 7/10 units and the upper arm is 3 6/10 units. Find the total length of the arm. Add in the two ways.
video_script.why: The child can order and change tenth numbers and now adds two lengths with units and tenths.
video_script.substitution: Add the units and the tenths separately, or change both to tenths and add the counts.
video_script.anchor: A jointed arm with a lower part and an upper part laid end to end along a unit scale
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the top numbers 7 + 6 = 13 and the bottom numbers 10 + 10 = 20 to get 13/20, but the parts stay tenths, so the count is 13 tenths.
video_script.payoff_line: The total length is six and three tenths units

names.Ruhee: the child whose arm is measured in two parts

maths_rules: 13 tenths = 10 tenths + 3 tenths = 1 unit + 3/10, so 5 + 1 = 6 units and 3/10 more.
Slip: 7 + 6 = 13 and 10 + 10 = 20 gives 13/20, but the part size stays one tenth.
video_script.design: One idea: parts of the same size are added by adding their counts, and the size stays tenths. Assumes the child can change units and tenths to tenths. Wrong idea: add the bottom numbers as well. The arm stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a lower arm of 2 7/10 units and an upper arm of 3 6/10 units laid end to end along a unit scale

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.lower: the lower arm appears on the scale, 2 7/10 units long
marks.upper: the upper arm appears after it, 3 6/10 units long
marks.ask: a bracket over both arms glows

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='lower'/>The lower arm of Ruhee is two and seven tenths units long.
<bookmark mark='upper'/>The upper arm is three and six tenths units long.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the total length of the arm, and can we add it in two ways?

beats.on_screen: the two arms stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a unit bar cut into 10 parts labelled 1/10; the 10 parts glow together as 1 unit

marks.same: the unit bar is cut into 10 parts, each labelled 1/10
marks.ten: the 10 parts glow together as 1 unit

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Parts of the same size can be counted together.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten tenths make one whole unit, so a big count of tenths can be turned into units.

beats.on_screen: Given: lower arm = 2 7/10 units, upper arm = 3 6/10 units
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the lower arm is two and seven tenths units long. The upper arm is three and six tenths units long.

beats.on_screen: To find: the total length, added in two ways

marks.find: the words added in two ways are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the total length, and add in two ways.

marks.one: the units and the tenths are split into two columns
marks.units: 2 + 3 = 5 is written in the units column
marks.tenths: 7/10 + 6/10 = 13/10 is written in the tenths column

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one is the first way, where we add the units and the tenths separately.
<bookmark mark='units'/>Two units and three units make five units.
<bookmark mark='tenths'/>Seven tenths and six tenths make thirteen tenths.

marks.join: the 1 unit joins the 5 units to make 6 units, with 3/10 left

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, thirteen tenths is ten tenths and three tenths, and ten tenths make one unit.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Five units and one unit make six units, and three tenths are left.

marks.three: the two lengths are lined up for changing
marks.conv: each length changes to a count of tenths

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three is the second way, where we change each length to tenths. <bookmark mark='conv'/>Two and seven tenths is twenty seven tenths. Three and six tenths is thirty six tenths.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Twenty seven tenths and thirty six tenths make sixty three tenths.

beats.on_screen: 63/10 = 60/10 + 3/10 = 6 units and 3/10, the same as the first way

marks.agree: the result is matched with the first way and an equals sign lands between them

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, change back. Sixty tenths is six units, and three tenths are still left over.
<bookmark mark='agree'/>This matches the answer from the first way.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The total length is six and three tenths units.
Both ways give the same answer.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 7/10 + 6/10 = 13/20; the 13 tenths bar shows 13 parts of size 1/10; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and 13 parts of size 1/10 glow

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven tenths and six tenths make thirteen twentieths. Keeko adds the top numbers and the bottom numbers.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the bottom number only names the size of the part. Both parts are tenths, so the size stays tenths. The count is thirteen tenths.
